key_insight: A fully automated pipeline can plan patient-specific iliosacral screw trajectories for reduced pelvic fractures by identifying safe corridors from 3D anatomy, reducing manual planning burden while improving safety.
engineering_relevance: This work supports faster and more reliable preoperative planning for minimally invasive pelvic fixation, where precise screw placement is critical to avoid neurovascular injury and failed fixation.
method: Uses patient-specific 3D anatomy from pelvic fracture cases
Combines statistical shape models with deep learning to detect safe screw corridors
Automatically generates individualized insertion trajectories for preoperative planning
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 200 clinical pelvic fracture cases, the method increased safe corridor margin by 2% across four screw types, cut planning time by over 90%, and achieved a 95% clinical acceptance rate.
watch_item: Performance may depend on image quality and anatomical variability, so robust validation across diverse fracture patterns and imaging protocols is important before broad clinical deployment.
paper_title: Automated Screw Planning for Reduced Pelvic Fractures Based on Statistical Shape Models and Deep Learning
